about.title: Welcome to Vibrosine
about.lead: A doctor’s sign might be hard to read, but not the sign of vibration. We help you understand what your machine is telling you.
story: Machine design and manufacturing, installation conditions and the way equipment operates can all make it challenging to identify the source of vibration. Lubricant properties also influence vibration behavior and rotating machinery performance.

Modern data acquisition systems, sensitive sensors, software and laboratory lubricant results are useful, but they still need to be interpreted with the right points in mind. Collecting useful data at the right time, place and operating condition helps lead to the most important part of the analysis: the root cause.

help.title: How can we help you?
items: Visit your plant, collect vibration data, analyze your machinery, report the findings and recommend appropriate corrective tasks.
Train your technicians and engineers in vibration data collection and analysis techniques so your team can work independently.
Guide students undertaking project work in vibration measurement and analysis.

team.title: Our team
team.body: Our engineers bring experience in oil and gas, manufacturing and process industries. Their work includes vibration analysis, modal testing, ODS (Operational Deflection Shape) analysis, dynamic balancing and field balancing. Training courses are developed for technicians, supervisors and engineers and can be tailored to specific requirements.

marketProspects.title: Market prospects
marketProspects.body: Processing plants need academically qualified and technically experienced people in condition monitoring, especially vibration measurement and analysis. As predictive maintenance becomes more widely understood, employers increasingly seek trained and internationally certified vibration analysts.
marketProspects.detail: Certification can help technical staff demonstrate their knowledge and be considered for condition-monitoring roles. Experienced staff also benefit from continuous training.
